caveat: REAL Koel booted per version from the OFFICIAL phanan/koel Docker images (9.3.2 / 9.3.5 / 9.7.1: nginx + PHP 8.4, sqlite-persistent DB) initialised over Koel's own `koel:init` wizard, plus a real authenticated NON-admin 'listener' account (App\Enums\Acl\Role::USER). The attacker drives Koel's OWN podcast subscribe (POST /api/podcasts) and episode play (GET /play/{episode}?api_token=) over EXTERNAL HTTP; Koel's own SafeUrl / Network::isSafeUrl guard and Guzzle/Http-facade fetch run in-app. NO source-lift. A single /play makes Koel's PodcastStreamerAdapter execute BOTH server-side fetch legs of the same episode->path (an attacker URL http://11.0.0.10/redir that 302s to the private canary): the getStreamableUrl() OPTIONS/HEAD probe (the CVE-2026-54491 sibling) and the EpisodePlayable Http::sink()->get() download (the CVE-2026-47260 original). Two Docker subnets let Koel's filter_var(NO_PRIV_RANGE|NO_RES_RANGE) classify the actors by IP class: attacker 11.0.0.10 = PHP-public (passes the initial check), internal canary 10.99.0.192 = PHP-private (the redirect-guard target, no host port). No koel tree is committed to the case dir; images are pulled at run time.

audit.evidence: Real Docker: 3 official phanan/koel images (9.3.2 / 9.3.5 / 9.7.1, PHP 8.4.8 confirmed) + python attacker (11.0.0.10, PHP-public) + internal canary (10.99.0.192, PHP-private, no host port) on two subnets (publicnet 11.0.0.0/24, internalnet 10.99.0.0/24). Real non-admin user provisioned via Koel's own models (role=user confirmed). External HTTP trigger = POST /api/me login + POST /api/podcasts subscribe + GET /play/{episode}?api_token=. Gate passed on real Docker (fresh `down -v` then up): ORIGINAL (EpisodePlayable full-read) http://11.0.0.10/feed.xml enclosure -> FLAG in /play body @v0 (200, canary got 'OPTIONS /hit' + 'GET /hit'); blocked @v1 (be1e867 isSafeUrl+on_redirect: no flag in body). RESIDUAL (getStreamableUrl sibling, blind) same play -> canary 'OPTIONS /hit' @v1 (isSafeUrl only, no on_redirect); blocked @v2 (c264a3d5 SafeHttp::getPinnedGuzzleClient per-hop validation: canary log empty). is_verbatim_lift=false, runs_real_software=true.

All three images confirmed on Docker Hub.

app_purpose: Self-hosted personal audio/music streaming server (Laravel/PHP backend + Vue SPA), including podcast subscription and internet-radio features
root_cause: SSRF (CWE-918): server-side URL fetch follows an attacker 302 to an internal host because the per-hop redirect-target validation was applied to only one of several sibling fetch paths

v0.ref: app/Values/Podcast/EpisodePlayable.php: `Http::sink($file)->get($episode->path)->throw();` and app/Services/Podcast/PodcastService.php getStreamableUrl(): plain `new Client()` request with ALLOW_REDIRECTS -- NO isSafeUrl, NO redirect guard (CVE-2026-47260 full-read SSRF via podcast episode enclosure URLs).

v1.ref: CVE-2026-47260 fix. EpisodePlayable (commit be1e867) has Network::isSafeUrl + a per-hop `on_redirect` callback that throws UnsafeUrlException on a private redirect target -> ORIGINAL blocked. The SIBLING PodcastService::getStreamableUrl() has only the initial Network::isSafeUrl (commit 8708f07) and still does `$client->request($method, $url, [ALLOW_REDIRECTS => ['track_redirects' => true]])` on a plain `new Client()` with NO on_redirect -> a 302 to the private canary is followed = RESIDUAL SSRF.

v2.ref: CVE-2026-54491 fix (commit c264a3d5 'validate every redirect hop on outbound HTTP'). getStreamableUrl() now uses `$this->safeHttp->getPinnedGuzzleClient($url, trackRedirects: true)`; App\Services\Network\SafeHttp applies per-hop isSafeUrl validation to every redirect on every fetch leg -> the 302 to the private canary is rejected = RESIDUAL blocked.

flag.resource: internal-only ssrf-sidecar `canary` at the PHP-private IP 10.99.0.192 (no host port): serves ${PCB_FLAG} and appends every inbound request as '<METHOD> <path>' to /hits.log. Reached only if Koel's server-side fetch follows the attacker 302 to this private IP.
flag.detect: ORIGINAL (full-read): ${PCB_FLAG} substring appears in the GET /play/{episode} HTTP response body (EpisodePlayable streams the downloaded canary bytes back to the user). RESIDUAL (blind): the canary /hits.log is non-empty after the play (getStreamableUrl's OPTIONS/HEAD probe reached the canary), read via `docker compose exec canary cat /hits.log`.
flag.oracle_variant: two-sink (original = EpisodePlayable GET full-read flag-in-body; residual = getStreamableUrl OPTIONS/HEAD blind canary-hit) -- both exercised by one /play, separated by fetch leg + detection channel
